summary:
Şanlıurfa stands under the national framework of Turkey, and the source inventory assembled for this province contains no trans-specific provincial material: no statute, enforcement action, facility, or incident recorded for Şanlıurfa itself. A trans visitor to the province is therefore governed by, and should expect, the Turkish national regime as documented here.

Human Rights Watch reported on 29 October 2025 that a leaked omnibus draft, the 11th Judicial Package, would amend the Turkish penal code to criminalise conduct deemed "contrary to biological sex and general morality", carrying up to three years in prison, and would criminalise participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies with up to four years. The same draft would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care, surgery included, from 18 to 25, behind a requirement of permanent infertility and repeated evaluations at government-approved hospitals. Healthcare professionals performing such interventions would face fines and up to seven years in prison, patients up to three years, with pretrial detention possible. Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association opposed the draft, and Human Rights Watch warns the measure would push treatment underground and leave LGBT people in constant fear of arrest.

Kaos GL's 2025 monitoring review, "The Year of the Family: A Major Siege Against LGBTI+ People", finds that hostility toward LGBTI+ people has become explicit state policy rather than residual prejudice. Public institutions received "Year of the Family" instructions, an LGBTI+ rights organisation was closed for the first time in years, expression and artistic freedom were restricted, and events were cancelled or banned.

The same review records 6 right-to-life violations including 3 hate-motivated killings, with transgender people the most affected group; 89 torture and ill-treatment violations, up from 51 the previous year; 313 liberty violations, roughly two and a half times the prior year's total, comprising 299 detention decisions; private-life violations rising from 16 to 67, among them obstruction of trans people's hormone therapy; and 61 travel bans.
tangentialFactors:
Both sources apply country-wide and carry no provincial breakdown, so neither supports any claim that Şanlıurfa is more or less exposed than Istanbul, Ankara, or any other Turkish province. The direction of travel across the national record is toward tightening: a draft that would criminalise conduct and raise the care threshold to 25 sits alongside a monitoring year in which liberty violations multiplied and private-life violations more than quadrupled.

The draft's pending status has not been treated as a suspension of hostility. Kaos GL documents institutional instruction and an organisational closure occurring in the same period the package remained unpassed, which indicates that the policy climate and the statute book are moving on separate clocks. For a visitor, the practical exposure is the enforcement climate, not only the text of any enacted measure.

Travel bans recorded at 61 in 2025 are a distinct category from the checkpoint document checks that affect foreigners, and the two should not be conflated: the former is a domestic judicial measure, the latter an identity-verification encounter in which presentation is compared against passport data.

outOfScopeNotes:
No province-specific trans-related source for Şanlıurfa was located in this inventory, so the province's own policing practice, local facilities, and any recorded incident remain unresolved and unsourced here. Characterisations of Şanlıurfa as exceptionally religious or tribal-conservative are not supported, contradicted, or scaled by any trans-specific provincial evidence in the sources reviewed, and are recorded as unverified.

Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been enacted, amended, or withdrawn since the Human Rights Watch report of 29 October 2025 is unresolved in this inventory; the sources establish its content and its pending status at that date only. Whether the Kayseri Provincial Health Directorate circular and the September 2025 Health Ministry regulation on "gender reassignment" reporting apply uniformly across provinces, including Şanlıurfa, is not stated in the sources reviewed.

Whether any Pride or LGBTI+ event has been held or banned in Şanlıurfa specifically is not sourced. The monitoring figures for 2025 are national totals and cannot be allocated to this province.
